name: Biological Chemistry
tagline: Enzymatic catalysis, biomolecular interactions, and the chemistry of life.
seo_title: Biological Chemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Biological Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in enzymes, proteins, nucleic acids, metabolism and chemical biology.

definition.lead: Biological chemistry, or biochemistry, explains life in molecular terms: how proteins, nucleic acids, lipids and sugars are built and how they react inside cells.
definition.body: Enzymes speed up reactions by factors of millions, DNA stores information, membranes control what enters a cell and metabolism turns food into usable energy. These molecules underlie modern medicine, biotechnology and drug discovery.

timeline.title: The first enzyme
timeline.text: Anselme Payen and Jean-François Persoz isolate diastase from barley.
timeline.why: The first enzyme to be described.

timeline.title: Cell-free fermentation
timeline.text: Eduard Buchner ferments sugar with an extract of yeast, without living cells.
timeline.why: Life's chemistry can be studied in a test tube.

timeline.title: Enzymes are proteins
timeline.text: James Sumner crystallizes the enzyme urease.
timeline.why: Settled the debate about what enzymes are made of.

timeline.title: The Krebs cycle
timeline.text: Hans Krebs describes the citric acid cycle.
timeline.why: The central hub of energy metabolism.

timeline.title: The double helix
timeline.text: Watson and Crick propose DNA's structure, using data from Franklin and Wilkins.
timeline.why: Explained how genetic information is copied.

timeline.title: Protein sequencing
timeline.text: Frederick Sanger completes the amino acid sequence of insulin.

timeline.title: Cracking the code
timeline.text: Marshall Nirenberg and Heinrich Matthaei decode the first codon.
timeline.why: The start of reading the genetic code.

timeline.title: PCR
timeline.text: Kary Mullis invents the polymerase chain reaction.
timeline.why: Copying DNA millions of times in hours.

timeline.title: CRISPR-Cas9
timeline.text: Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna show Cas9 can be programmed to cut DNA.
timeline.why: Genome editing became simple; Nobel Prize in 2020.

timeline.title: mRNA vaccines
timeline.text: Nobel Prize in Medicine to Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman for nucleoside modifications.
